title: Frozen evaluable-only corpus baseline
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want a frozen, citable baseline of per-layer scores on **evaluable (read) cases only**, so that later scanner changes are compared to one snapshot instead of mixed unread and alias noise.

## Current gap

`pnpm run benchmark:run` can print per-layer recall/precision/unread, but:

- It is opt-in, not CI. CI does not materialize 29 upstream clones.
- Nobody has published the post-harness-fix numbers on scanner `develop` as the official baseline (the last full run was against the CLI copy, with the old mixed-bag runner).
- Packets with high unread (PHP/Ruby/Swift/Rust evidence) will dominate any “overall recall” that is not sliced.
- Plexus accuracy/recall was not a successful baseline (proxy `trusted_open` / missing `evaluate_recall`).
- Fixture Jest is already green and too small to steer corpus work.

Without a baseline, every agent will re-run a slightly different command (`--include-proposed`, different materialized cache, CLI vs scanner) and argue from incomparable tables.

## Questions to answer

- Official command, repo, branch, gold review_state (`accepted` only), and whether AI inference is off (must be off for deterministic headline).
- Required columns: packet, layer, evaluable positives, recall, label accuracy, precision, unread count, unread rate. Overall = sum of denominators, not average of percents.
- Do we publish a committed artifact (JSON/Markdown under `tests/benchmark/` or Kanbus wiki) and update it only on gold or scorer contract changes — never on detector tweaks?
- Language slice: a second table restricted to extensions ingest actually reads, so unread-heavy packets do not hide Python/TS/Go signal?
- How do `documentedGap` cases appear (in recall, excluded from CI gates, listed)?
- Materialize in CI or only locally? If locally, how do we authenticate “this baseline was produced from these SHAs”?

## Depends on

Tasks 1–5 should land as *decisions* first, or the baseline will be thrown out when unread/identity/layers change. This task can still specify the *shape* of the report in parallel.

## Not this task

Do not start a scanner improvement loop from an unpublished CLI run. Do not cite Plexus until it uses `scoreEvalCases` (or an agreed identical contract).

comments.author: home
claude
comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## Agreed this lands last — and the report needs a column the questions do not ask for

The "Depends on" note is right, and the review of tasks 1-5 strengthens it: a baseline published today would be a table of artefacts. Concretely, of 1,792 annotations:

- **563 component** cases score near 0 because gold uses taxonomy subtypes and the engine emits instance names (KDATAP-08a0ac);
- **436 data-flow** cases cannot match at all — bare prose endpoints against a nested-component-key grammar;
- **213 of 357 mention** cases match only through the `identity.ts` alias table;
- **422** mention + data-item cases match no rule under any alias;
- **960 of 1,792** sit on files ingest cannot open.

Publishing that as "the baseline" would hand every future session a number where the dominant term is vocabulary mismatch.

### The missing column: reachability

The requested columns (packet, layer, evaluable positives, recall, label accuracy, precision, unread count, unread rate) still cannot distinguish three different zeros:

1. a rule/detector exists and missed it — **a scanner problem**;
2. no rule or detector concept exists for this gold at all — **a taxonomy-coverage problem**;
3. gold and engine name the same thing differently — **a vocabulary problem**.

Today all three land in the recall denominator as "miss". Recommend the report carry **`reachable`** alongside `evaluablePositives`: the count of read positives whose subject the engine could in principle emit. Then publish `recall` over reachable, and `coverage = reachable / evaluable` as its own number. With today's rules that would read ~68% ceiling on mentions and ~29% on data items — which is the fact a future session most needs, and the one a single recall percentage hides.

### Answers to the rest

- **Official command / repo / branch:** `pnpm run benchmark:run` on `DataParade-io/scanner` `develop`, `review_state: accepted` only (the default in `to-eval-cases.ts`; note `precision.ts` currently ignores it and counts the 75 `proposed` annotations — see KDATAP-89d1a6). AI inference off: `createDefaultScanConfiguration({ enableAiInference: false })` is already hard-coded in `scan-repo.ts`, so the deterministic headline is the only thing that path can produce. Recommend asserting it rather than relying on it.
- **Overall = sum of denominators, not average of percents** — agreed, and with 288-annotation discourse next to 5-annotation ory-kratos-password the difference is not cosmetic. Recommend also refusing to print a single cross-layer "overall" at all; the four layers measure different things and one number invites exactly the citation the epic is trying to prevent.
- **Committed artifact, updated only on gold or scorer contract changes, never on detector tweaks** — agreed, and this is the load-bearing rule of the whole task. Recommend the artifact record the SHAs it was produced from (scanner commit + the 29 `manifest.yaml` commits) in the file itself, which also answers the authentication question below.
- **Language slice** — yes, and prefer it over the unsliced table as the default view. Restrict to extensions `getFileLanguage` returns non-undefined for. Without it, wordpress/magento/discourse/spree/redmine/drupal/vapor dominate any aggregate.
- **`documentedGap`** — cannot appear today: `annotationToEvalCase` does not copy it, `AnnotationExpected` has no field for it, and **0 of 1,792** annotations set it. This task should not assume the mechanism exists. Recommend either adding it to the corpus schema as part of KDATAP-89d1a6, or dropping it from the report shape and using the `reachable` split instead — which I think is the better answer, since a gap with a denominator is more useful than a gap with a flag.
- **Materialize in CI or locally?** Locally. 29 upstream clones in CI buys little while the contracts are open. Authenticate the baseline by recording SHAs in the artifact, plus `validateMaterializedRepo` already checking the materialized tree against `manifest.commit`.

### Sequencing

Recommend this task **specify the report shape now** (columns, slices, the `reachable` definition, the artifact location and its SHA block) and **produce no numbers** until KDATAP-d6eabf, KDATAP-791091 and KDATAP-08a0ac have decisions. A shape agreed in advance is also the cheapest way to stop the next agent inventing a fourth table.

Agreed on the boundary: no baseline from an unpublished CLI run, no citing Plexus until it uses `scoreEvalCases`.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Three report states the field list does not yet distinguish

Agreed on freezing only after tasks 1-5, on immutable contract-versioned series, and on the fingerprint set. Three additions from measuring what the first artifact would actually contain.

### 1. Reachability, as a diagnostic denominator

There are 15 rules in `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml`. **422 of 793** mention and data-item gold cases match no rule under any name — not an alias problem, no detector concept exists. Ceilings with today's rules, perfect matching assumed: **~68% mention recall, ~29% data-item recall.**

These cases are eligible (file read successfully) and permanently missed, so no eligibility reason describes them. KDATAP-08a0ac rightly rejects excluding known gaps from raw metrics, and this does not ask for that: **`reachable` sits beside `evaluablePositives` as a reported diagnostic, and raw recall still counts every miss.** Without it, the first published data-item figure reads as detector quality when it is dominated by 308 gold entries keyed on source field names (`id`, `uid`, `uuid`, `status`, `key`).

### 2. "Precision not computable" is distinct from precision null

Under the eligibility decision, precision scope = reviewed packet-and-layer scope ∩ files successfully processed for that layer. Today's scope lives on 434 positive annotations, ~18.9k entries dominated by `.php` (~6.5k) and `.rb` (~6.0k), and ingest opens none of those extensions.

For discourse, wordpress, magento, redmine, spree, drupal and vapor — **7 of 29 packets, 54% of all annotations** — the intersection is close to empty. Precision there is not low and not zero-findings-in-scope; it is **not computable**. Recommend an explicit state so the Markdown rendering cannot present it as `null` alongside "scope declared, no findings", and so no release gate is written against packets that structurally cannot produce the number.

Same distinction is needed for data flows if they publish before regold — see KDATAP-08a0ac, where the recommendation is to report them as unscorable pending regold rather than as a 0% strict layer.

### 3. The first series has no predecessor to bridge from

The bridge-run rule assumes an old contract to run alongside the new one. There isn't one on scanner `develop`: `benchmark:run` has never been executed here as a published baseline, the last full run was against the `dataparade-cli` copy with the pre-fix mixed runner, and `precision.ts` — the only other scorer — has the layer-scope defect noted on KDATAP-89d1a6, so its numbers are wrong in a known direction.

Recommend the artifact schema allow a series with `predecessor: none` and that the first baseline say so explicitly, rather than a bridge run being attempted against a source that would only manufacture a false continuity.

### Notes on the required fields

- Deterministic configuration with AI disabled is already structural rather than optional: `scan-repo.ts` hard-codes `createDefaultScanConfiguration({ enableAiInference: false })`. Recommend asserting it in the artifact rather than relying on it, since the CLI path does not share that constraint.
- Accepted-gold-only matches the `to-eval-cases.ts` default (`DEFAULT_REVIEW_STATES = ["accepted"]`). Current counts: **1,717 accepted, 75 proposed**, 1,565 positive / 173 negative / 54 ambiguous. Worth recording those four counts in the first artifact as the corpus fingerprint baseline.
- Materialization validation already exists in `validateMaterializedRepo` against `manifest.commit`; the artifact needs the resulting SHAs, not a re-implementation.
- The language/capability slice is the load-bearing view here, not a supplement. With 7 packets contributing almost no eligible evidence, the unsliced table's denominators are dominated by supported-language packets anyway — the slice is what makes that legible rather than accidental.

### Sequencing

Recommend this task produce the **schema and rendering now** — field list, states, series identity, fingerprint block — and no numbers until 1-5 are implemented. A schema agreed in advance is also the cheapest defence against the fourth ad-hoc table the decision rejects.
